FIELD JOURNALS
THREE NOTABLE CLOSES FROM FY24
WELCOMING THE LINE ON THE MARSH
Holding the line on the Cardigan Bay marsh edge.

Year three of monitoring shows accretion meeting and exceeding the 2022 model. We submitted the raw cores to the journal in November.

VIA FORTUNES ACTIVITY REVIEWS
Six Forensic survey returns 1,672 ha to tidal exchange.

Coordinated breach across the eastern bund. We waited eight years for the planning permission and another two for the spring tides to confirm the design.

PEAT HYDROLOGY RESTORED
Peat hydrology restored across the Lithens headwaters.

Forty kilometres of new bunds and 412 dams. The water table is back within 6 cm of surface for the first time since the 1960s.

METHODOLOGY
HOW WE MEASURE WHAT WE MEASURE
01
Field measurement.

Every site runs a quarterly transect protocol — cores, surveys, water-table loggers. Raw data is published with every quarterly entry. No third-party aggregator sits between the measurement and the page.

02
Financial reconciliation.

Every transaction over €25 is recorded in the ledger with vendor, date, project, and the staff signoff. Auditor reviews monthly. CSV available.

03
Carbon accounting.

We do not sell offsets. We do not trade credits. Carbon stocks are recorded as a benefit of the work, not as the currency. The ledger reports stocks against the IPCC 2019 refinement.

04
Community signoff.

Every project enrolls the surrounding community as named contributors. Crew lists are public. Local fieldwork hours are surfaced quarterly.
